title: Longitudinal multimodal cardiovascular imaging study
purpose: Assess whether Standard preserves mixed historical/prospective longitudinal uncertainty and navigates multimodal imaging, measurement, analysis and data implications without silently adopting a design.
initialUserIntent: We have historical cardiac MRI and echocardiography data from patients followed after a first myocardial infarction, and we can prospectively recruit new patients with follow-up imaging. We want to understand adverse left ventricular remodeling, but the exact study design, timing, primary endpoint, and role of each imaging modality are not decided.

knownFacts.statement: Historical cardiac MRI data are available.
The historical patients were followed after a first myocardial infarction.
Prospective recruitment of new patients with follow-up imaging is feasible.
The scientific aim is to understand adverse left ventricular remodeling.

unresolvedDecisions.statement: Exact study design and the relationship between historical and prospective components.
Scientific role and hierarchy of MRI and echocardiography.
Handling of temporal, site and acquisition heterogeneity if multiple sites are involved.

outOfScopeInformation: Exact acquisition parameters are not part of the fixture.
Reader organization and equipment equivalence are not supplied.
No jurisdiction-specific or product-specific regulatory fact is supplied.
allowedClarifications: Clarify whether historical and prospective participants belong to one inferential population or distinct components.
Clarify the intended primary scientific objective or endpoint without presupposing one.
Clarify complementary or hierarchical modality roles.
Clarify site structure, acquisition provenance and comparability constraints.

conditionalOwners.condition: Only if later adopted Project facts create a material regulatory applicability question.

terminalTarget: A coherent versioned Research Project preserving unresolved decisions, with current Protocol/TMP/DOC projection reachable after the necessary human adoptions.
